the mass function of cluster galaxies evolves with redshift, that the mass function and the morphology-mass relations of different morphological populations evolve, and that the evolution of the morphology-mass distribution is mainly driven by star formation.

the stellar mass function in clusters is not universal, but it strongly evolves with redshift, and it is driven by the evolution of late-type galaxies, which are the main source of new stellar mass in clusters.
the galaxy mass function in clusters evolves with time.

the evolution in the mass function of clusters between z ∼ 1 and 0 is mainly due to mass growth through star formation and morphological transformations.

the observed mass function of galaxies in clusters at z ∼ 1 is the result of the combined effects of star formation and infalling galaxies, and the evolution of the mass function is the result of these two effects acting in concert.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass function of clusters is a result of the interplay between star formation and infalling processes.
the mass function of galaxies in clusters has been shaped by a combination of star formation, mass growth, and morphological transformation.

the evolution of the cluster galaxy population is driven by a complex interplay between the different mechanisms that shape the mass function.
